transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve been eating a lot more than I mean to sometimes. After a long day on site, or after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll get home and just eat whatever’s there—leftover takeout, cereal, chips—until I’m really uncomfortably full.
During those times, do you feel unable to stop eating once you’ve started?
Yeah. Once I start, it feels like I’m on autopilot. I’m telling myself to stop, especially because I’ve got an early crew start, but I still keep going back to the kitchen for more.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo them?
A few times a month, yeah. Afterward I panic and go to the bathroom and make myself throw up, because I feel like I need to undo it—especially with how much effort I put into looking put-together.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?

A lot, honestly. Since I’ve been wearing more fitted work clothes and being more visible at meetings, I kind of judge the whole day by whether my pants feel tight or if I think people can see my stomach.
Besides making yourself vomit, do you do anything else to try to prevent weight gain after these eating episodes?
I’m not really sure what else you mean. Mostly it’s the vomiting afterward when I panic.
About how often do you make yourself vomit after these eating episodes?
A few times a month, usually after those nights. I panic and feel like I have to undo it.
About how often do these binge-eating episodes happen in a typical week?
Looking back over the last few months, it’s probably averaged about once a week. Some weeks it happens twice, and then other weeks not at all.
Is your body weight currently much lower than what’s considered healthy for your height?
I’m not sure what would count as healthy for my height. I haven’t really been told that my weight is much lower than it should be.
Over the last 3 months, how often have you made yourself vomit after eating?
Over the last three months, it’s averaged about once a week. Some weeks it’s happened twice, and other weeks not at all.
